proposed_widenings.name: magic_vehicle / item_locomotion
proposed_widenings.justification: The carpet itself gains fly speed and moves as a pilotable vehicle; the rider is a passenger, not the subject of a grant_speed atom. No existing family or atom models an item acquiring its own movement mode and carrying passengers.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You can make this carpet hover and fly by taking a Magic action and using the carpet's command word. It moves according to your directions if you are within 30 feet of it.

proposed_widenings.name: item_command_radius on ActivatedAbilityMechanics or a new vehicle family
proposed_widenings.justification: The carpet responds to directional commands only when the commander is within 30 ft. No surface field expresses a remote-control radius for an item's ongoing movement.
proposed_widenings.evidence: It moves according to your directions if you are within 30 feet of it.

proposed_widenings.name: weight_capacity predicate for conditional speed modification
proposed_widenings.justification: The carpet's fly speed is halved when carrying more than its normal capacity (up to 2× capacity). No existing EquipmentPredicate or OngoingPredicate models a cargo-weight threshold.
proposed_widenings.evidence: A carpet can carry up to twice the weight shown on the table, but its Fly Speed is halved if it carries more than its normal capacity.

notes: The four size variants (3×5, 4×6, 5×7, 6×9 ft) with different capacities and fly speeds (80/60/40/30 ft) could be expressed via MagicItemRecord.variants once the core vehicle mechanic exists. The d100 GM-random size selection is DM agenda (GM picks or rolls). The fundamental blocker is the item-as-vehicle pattern: grant_speed targets a creature, but the carpet IS the flying entity. Encoding as 'rider gains fly speed' would be dishonest — the carpet can fly without a rider aboard and the speed halving is cargo-weight-based, not rider-weight-based.
